title: Leads, conversion, accounts, contacts, person accounts, opportunities, products, price books, quotes, and campaigns
objectives: Explain Lead as a pre-relationship sales record and conversion as the official handoff that creates or matches Account, Contact (or Person Account), and optionally Opportunity.
Choose business Account plus Contact versus Person Account from Company data and org enablement, not from a UI preference.
Place Products, Price Books, Quotes, and Campaigns on the path from catalog and marketing to a priced deal.
Separate sales-object metadata (record types, field maps, price books) from business records (a LAB_ lead or opportunity row).
diagnostic_question: A website inquiry has a name, email, and no company. A second inquiry has a company and wants a priced proposal. Before converting anything, which objects do you create, and what would conversion vs a Person Account vs a Quote change?
definition: Sales Cloud models the path from an unqualified inquiry to a priced deal: a Lead is captured and later converted into an Account and Contact (or a Person Account when Company is blank and Person Accounts are enabled), optionally with an Opportunity. Products live in Price Books so they can be added to Opportunities; Quotes formalize an offer; Campaigns group members for marketing. ([Lead Settings](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.customize_leadsettings.htm); [Web-to-Lead](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.customize_leadpreparation.htm); [Add Products to Opportunities](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.products_add.htm); [Create Custom Price Books](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.pricebooks_create.htm))
why_it_matters: Interviewers fail candidates who treat Lead as a second Account, who convert every website hit into an Opportunity, or who add Products without a Price Book. Wrong Person Account vs business Account choice is hard to unwind. Campaign membership and quote lines also break reporting if the objects are used as dumping grounds.
sixty_second_explanation: Picture a freight depot. A Lead is a crate still in receiving—interesting, not yet a customer. Conversion is customs clearance: the crate becomes a consignee company (Account) plus a named recipient (Contact), or one household shipment (Person Account) when there is no company. An Opportunity is the booked lane. Products are SKUs; Price Books are rate cards; a Quote is the printed offer; a Campaign is a seasonal promo that tags crates and recipients as members.
deeper_explanation: Lead Settings in Setup control default owner, conversion options such as Preserve Lead Status, merge, and related notifications. Conversion is an org behavior, not a one-off page layout trick. ([Lead Settings](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.customize_leadsettings.htm))

Web-to-Lead generates leads from a website and is documented at up to 500 new leads a day. Custom lead fields should be mapped to Account, Contact, and Opportunity fields before conversion. Assignment rules and a default owner cover leads that miss rule criteria. ([Web-to-Lead](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.customize_leadpreparation.htm))

When Person Accounts are enabled, Company is no longer universally required on Lead. A lead with a Company value converts to a business Account plus Contact; a lead with a blank Company converts to a Person Account. Do not invent a third conversion target. (Needs verification of the exact Person Accounts enablement path in the target edition; treat enablement as one-way until Help for that org is rechecked.)

Opportunity products require Read on Products and Price Books and Edit on Opportunities. The first product forces a Price Book choice; list price comes from the Price Book entry and can be overridden as sales price. Custom Price Books exist so each market segment can have its own prices. Quotes are edition- and license-gated; do not assume Quotes exist in every org. ([Add Products to Opportunities](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.products_add.htm); [Create Custom Price Books](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.pricebooks_create.htm))

Campaigns are marketing containers. Members are leads, contacts, or person accounts—not opportunities. Opportunity is the revenue object; Campaign Influence and member status belong to later marketing design, not this lesson's object map.

mental_model.analogy: A freight depot: receiving crate (Lead), customs clearance (conversion), consignee company (Account), named recipient (Contact), household shipment (Person Account), booked lane (Opportunity), SKU catalog (Products), lane rate card (Price Book), printed offer (Quote), seasonal promo list (Campaign).
useful_mapping: Lead → crate still in receiving, not yet a customer
conversion → customs clearance that creates or matches downstream records
Contact → a named person at that company
Person Account → one household record when there is no company
Product → a SKU; Price Book → the rate card that prices it
Quote → a printed offer, often tied to an Opportunity
Campaign → a promo roster of leads/contacts/person accounts
where_it_breaks: Conversion can match existing Account/Contact instead of always creating new rows.
Person Accounts are an org-wide data model, not a record-type costume on Contact.
A Quote is not a Price Book and not a Campaign.
The depot does not encode sharing, duplicate rules, or CPQ.

teach_back_prompt: Walk a Java developer through Lead versus Account/Contact versus Person Account, then say why converting every web inquiry into an Opportunity is the wrong default.

review_schedule.prompt: From memory: what does conversion create, and when does it create a Person Account instead of Account plus Contact?
Given a website hit, a named company deal, and a priced proposal request, pick Lead, Account/Contact, Opportunity, Product/Price Book, Quote, or Campaign.
Explain why the first Opportunity Product requires a Price Book, and what a custom Price Book is for.
Troubleshoot a converted lead whose custom fields did not land on Account.
Two-minute interview: sales object map plus one Person Account trap.

claims.claim: Lead Settings in Setup define default lead owner and conversion-related options such as Preserve Lead Status.
claims.validation: Define Default Settings for Lead Creation.

claims.claim: Web-to-Lead can generate up to 500 new leads a day. Custom lead fields should be mapped for conversion to Account, Contact, and Opportunity. Inactive assignment rules send web leads to the default owner in Lead Settings.
Adding opportunity products requires Edit on opportunities and Read on products and price books. The first product chooses a price book; sales price defaults from the price book list price.

Custom price books hold segment-specific prices. Quotes are not available in every edition; Help lists Quotes as Performance and Developer, and as Professional, Enterprise, and Unlimited with Sales Cloud.
claims.scope: Price books and Quotes edition gate
claims.validation: Create Custom Price Books edition table.

changed_in_release: Reverify Lead Settings labels, Web-to-Lead daily cap, and Quotes edition gates against Summer '26 Help in the target org.
unresolved_uncertainty: Exact Person Accounts enablement and irreversibility wording should be re-read in current Help for the org's edition before stating 'cannot be disabled' in an interview as a hard guarantee.
Campaign Influence, CPQ, and Revenue Cloud quoting are neighboring products; do not treat them as standard Opportunity Products.

telugu_glossary.telugu: వెబ్‌సైట్ విచారణను కస్టమర్ రికార్డులుగా మార్చే అధికారిక అడుగు.
కంపెనీ లేని వ్యక్తి కోసం Account మరియు Contact కలిసిన ఒక రికార్డు.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: A Lead is not a customer yet. Conversion creates or matches Account and Contact, or a Person Account when Company is blank and Person Accounts are on. Opportunity is the deal. Products need a Price Book. Quotes are a formal offer. Campaigns hold members, not revenue.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I start from qualification. Website noise stays a Lead; Web-to-Lead is capped and needs field maps plus assignment. I convert only when sales owns a relationship. Company present means business Account plus Contact; blank Company with Person Accounts means Person Account. I create an Opportunity only if there is a deal to forecast. First product forces a Price Book. I do not use a Campaign as a fake Opportunity or a Quote as a Price Book.

terminology.plain: Someone who showed interest but is not yet a customer record in the account model.
terminology.precise: A sales object used to capture and nurture inquiries. Web-to-Lead can create up to 500 leads a day. Conversion, not a report, is how a lead becomes Account/Contact or Person Account.
terminology.example: LAB_ web form creates Lead LAB_Maya with email and no company.
terminology.non_example: An Account named LAB_Maya stored because 'we always use Account.'
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Contact: a person already tied to a customer Account (or a Person Account).
terminology.boundary: Duplicate matching and scoring products are neighboring, not this object's definition.

terminology.plain: The official action that turns a qualified Lead into customer records.
terminology.precise: Lead conversion creates or matches Account and Contact, or a Person Account, and can create an Opportunity. Custom Lead fields must be mapped beforehand. Lead Settings control conversion options such as Preserve Lead Status.
terminology.example: Convert LAB_Maya after a discovery call; map LAB_Source__c to Account.
terminology.non_example: Manually typing the same person as a Contact without converting, leaving a duplicate Lead.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Lead Status picklist change without Convert is not conversion.
terminology.boundary: Automation that fires on convert is AUTO-001; this lesson is the object outcome.

terminology.plain: The company (or household, if Person Accounts) you sell to.
terminology.precise: The customer or partner organization record. Business Accounts hold Contacts. Person Accounts collapse person and account into one record when enabled.
terminology.example: LAB_Northwind Traders as the consignee company after conversion.
terminology.non_example: A Lead still sitting in receiving used as the 'company' in reports.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Person Account: not a child of Account; it is a different account model.
terminology.boundary: Account teams and territory assignment are APP-002.

terminology.plain: A named person who belongs to a business Account.
terminology.precise: A person record related to a business Account. On conversion with a Company value, Salesforce creates or matches this person. Campaign members may be contacts.
terminology.example: LAB_Maya Patel, Email, related to LAB_Northwind Traders.
terminology.non_example: A Person Account treated as if it also needed a separate Contact row for the same human.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Lead: pre-relationship person; Contact is post-conversion (or direct create).
terminology.boundary: Contact roles on Opportunity are a related list, not a second person object.

terminology.plain: One record for a person who is the customer, used when you sell to people not companies.
terminology.precise: When Person Accounts are enabled, leads without Company convert to Person Accounts; leads with Company convert to business Accounts. Company is not universally required on Lead in that model.
terminology.example: B2C gym membership: convert blank-Company Lead LAB_Maya to a Person Account.
terminology.non_example: Renaming a business Account record type 'Person' without enabling Person Accounts.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Contact: still the B2B person-on-a-company model.
terminology.boundary: Enablement steps and irreversibility: Needs verification in current Help for the org.

terminology.plain: A deal you are working that can produce revenue.
terminology.precise: The revenue object in the sales path. Conversion may create one; it should not be automatic for every lead. Products attach after a Price Book is chosen.
terminology.example: LAB_Northwind Q3 Widgets, Stage Prospecting, Amount from products.
terminology.non_example: A Campaign named 'Q3 Widgets' used as the only place the deal is tracked.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Quote: a proposed offer, often child of an Opportunity, not a substitute for pipeline.
terminology.boundary: Sales process and forecast category mapping are APP-002.

terminology.plain: A SKU you sell, priced through a Price Book.
terminology.precise: Catalog item. Adding it to an Opportunity requires Read on products and price books. Quantity and sales price are stored on the opportunity product.
terminology.example: LAB_Widget SKU on Standard Price Book, quantity 10, sales price 50.
terminology.non_example: Typing the product name only in Opportunity Description.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Price Book Entry: the priced row for that product in a specific book.
terminology.boundary: Schedules and CPQ bundles are later/adjacent.

terminology.plain: A rate card: which products at which list prices for a market.
terminology.precise: Standard and custom price books. Custom books serve segments (domestic vs international). Active books can be used on opportunities or quotes. The first opportunity product selects the book.
terminology.example: LAB_Domestic 2026 custom price book with Widget list price 50.
terminology.non_example: A spreadsheet emailed to reps with no Price Book records.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Quote: customer-facing offer that may pull from a Price Book, not the book itself.
terminology.boundary: Quotes edition availability is listed in Price Book Help.

terminology.plain: A formal offer you can send, usually from an Opportunity.
terminology.precise: Quote records and line items. Help states Quotes are available in Performance and Developer Editions and in Professional, Enterprise, and Unlimited with Sales Cloud. Not a Campaign.
terminology.example: LAB_Northwind Quote v2 synced from opportunity products.
terminology.non_example: A Chatter post with a dollar amount called 'the quote.'
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Opportunity Amount: pipeline number, not the customer PDF/offer record.
terminology.boundary: CPQ/Revenue Cloud quote lifecycle is a different product family.

terminology.plain: A marketing program roster, not the deal itself.
terminology.precise: A container whose members are leads, contacts, or person accounts. Use it to track who was targeted, not to replace Opportunity pipeline.
terminology.example: LAB_Spring Promo campaign with Lead LAB_Maya as a member.
terminology.non_example: Creating an Opportunity for every email click instead of Campaign membership.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: List View: a query, not a membership object with campaign member statuses.
terminology.boundary: Campaign Influence ROI math is a later reporting topic.

mechanics.after: Lead created (Web-to-Lead or manual) with assignment or default owner
mechanics.observe: LAB_ lead in the queue or on the default owner
mechanics.failure: Creating an Account for every form submit

mechanics.trigger: Custom fields or Person Account model in play
mechanics.after: Lead field maps saved; Company blank vs populated understood
mechanics.observe: Map Lead Fields shows LAB_ custom fields
mechanics.failure: Converting first and wondering why Account is empty

mechanics.after: Account/Contact or Person Account; Opportunity only if there is a deal
mechanics.observe: Converted Lead related records; no extra Opportunity for a newsletter signup

mechanics.trigger: Need SKUs, an offer, or a program
mechanics.after: Price Book chosen, products added, Quote if licensed, Campaign members for marketing
mechanics.observe: Opportunity Products related list; Campaign member row

when_to_use: When an inbound person is not yet a customer and must start as a Lead rather than an Account.
When conversion should create Account and Contact, or a Person Account if Company is blank and Person Accounts are enabled.
When an Opportunity needs Products from a Price Book instead of a typed amount only.
When a Quote is the customer-facing offer and a Campaign is the marketing roster of leads, contacts, or person accounts.
when_not_to_use: Do not convert every Web-to-Lead inquiry into an Opportunity when there is no deal to forecast.
Do not model B2C people as business Accounts plus dummy Contacts if the org's Person Accounts design is the approved model.
Do not add Opportunity Products without choosing a Price Book, or assume Quotes exist in every edition.
Do not use a Campaign as a substitute for Accounts, Contacts, or pipeline Opportunities.
configuration_or_code_location: Setup → Lead Settings (default owner, conversion options).
Setup → Object Manager → Lead → Map Lead Fields.
Setup → Web-to-Lead HTML generation; assignment rules for Lead.
Price Books tab; Opportunity Products related list; Quotes if licensed; Campaigns tab.

worked_example.scenario: Sandbox lab: LAB_ gym sells B2C memberships and a small B2B corporate package. A website form creates leads (max documented 500/day). One submit has no company (Maya). One has Company LAB_Northwind and wants a priced corporate package. Person Accounts are enabled. No production data.
inputs: Web-to-Lead form with Last Name, Email, optional Company
Custom LAB_Channel__c on Lead mapped to Account
Standard Price Book plus LAB_Corporate 2026 custom price book

decisions.decision: Leave Maya as a Lead until a trial class is booked; convert with blank Company to a Person Account; do not create an Opportunity for a newsletter-only submit.
decisions.because: Blank Company with Person Accounts converts to Person Account. Opportunity is for a deal.

decisions.decision: Convert the Northwind lead to business Account plus Contact and an Opportunity, then choose LAB_Corporate 2026 and add LAB_CorporatePack.
decisions.because: Company is present. First product requires a price book. Sales price defaults from list price.
decisions.rejected: Type the package price only on Opportunity Amount

decisions.decision: Add both people as members of Campaign LAB_Spring Promo; create a Quote only for Northwind if Quotes are licensed in this org.
decisions.because: Campaigns hold members. Quotes are edition-gated per Price Book Help.
decisions.rejected: Store the promo audience as Opportunities

configuration_or_code: Lead Settings: default owner = LAB_Queue or a sandbox user; review Preserve Lead Status.
Map LAB_Channel__c Lead → Account before converting.
Convert Maya (no Company) and Northwind (Company) in sandbox and compare resulting objects.
On Northwind Opportunity: Add Products → select LAB_Corporate 2026 → add LAB_CorporatePack.
worked_example.output: Maya is a Person Account without a junk Opportunity. Northwind is Account+Contact+Opportunity with a price-booked product. Campaign members exist for both.
verification: Converted Maya has no Company Account duplicate; it is a Person Account.
Northwind Opportunity Products shows the custom price book and list/sales price.
Unmapped if you remove the field map: Account LAB_Channel__c stays blank after a fresh convert test.
worked_example.self_explanation: I used Company presence to choose Person Account vs business Account. I used Price Book for SKUs and Campaign for marketing, not as fake deals.

hands_on_lab.environment: Disposable Developer sandbox or Trailhead Playground; synthetic LAB_ records only.
starting_state_checks: You can create Leads, Accounts, and Opportunities.
Confirm whether Person Accounts are already enabled before changing anything irreversible.
steps: Create Lead LAB_NoCompany (blank Company) and Lead LAB_WithCompany (Company LAB_Northwind).
Map one custom Lead field if you can create custom fields; otherwise note the Map Lead Fields screen.
Convert both leads; create an Opportunity only for LAB_WithCompany.
On that Opportunity, add a Product after selecting a Price Book; add both converted people to a LAB_ campaign as members.
guided_completion: If both converts created business Accounts, Person Accounts are not enabled—do not force-enable in a shared org without approval.
If Add Products is missing, check Read on products and price books.
hands_on_lab.independent_challenge: Explain to a teammate why Web-to-Lead at 500/day still needs a default owner when assignment rules are inactive.
evidence: Notes showing object types created for blank vs populated Company.
Opportunity Products screenshot with a Price Book named (LAB_ only).
stop_recovery_cleanup: Delete LAB_ leads, accounts, opportunities, products, and campaigns from the sandbox.
Do not enable Person Accounts in production from this lab.
hands_on_lab.limitations: This lab does not prove Campaign Influence, CPQ, or production Web-to-Lead volume.

decision_table.signal: Website or event inquiry, not yet a customer, may need assignment and a 500/day web cap.
decision_table.choose: Create or keep a Lead (Web-to-Lead plus assignment or default owner).
decision_table.not: An Account and Opportunity for every form submit.
decision_table.why: Lead Settings and Web-to-Lead Help treat Lead as the capture object before conversion.

decision_table.signal: Qualified human with a Company name; Person Accounts may or may not be on.
decision_table.choose: Convert to business Account plus Contact; Opportunity only if there is a deal.
decision_table.not: A Person Account while Company is populated.
decision_table.why: Company-bearing leads convert to the business account model.

decision_table.signal: Qualified B2C human, Person Accounts enabled, Company blank.
decision_table.choose: Convert to a Person Account; skip Opportunity if there is no deal.
decision_table.not: A dummy business Account named after the person plus a dummy Contact.
decision_table.why: Blank Company with Person Accounts is the documented convert path to Person Account.

decision_table.signal: Rep must sell SKUs with segment list prices on the Opportunity.
decision_table.choose: Activate a custom Price Book and add Opportunity Products from it.
decision_table.not: Typing SKUs only in Description or Amount.
decision_table.why: Add Products Help requires a price book on first product and Read on products and price books.

decision_table.signal: Need a customer-facing priced offer versus a marketing audience list.
decision_table.choose: Quote for the offer if the edition includes Quotes; Campaign members for the audience.
decision_table.not: Using Campaign as the quote or Quote as the campaign roster.
decision_table.why: Price Book Help gates Quotes; Campaigns hold leads/contacts/person accounts, not quote lines.

limitations: Does not teach Collaborative Forecasts, sales processes, or territories (APP-002).
Does not teach CPQ or Revenue Cloud quote engines.
Person Account enablement details are edition-specific; reverify Help.
Web-to-Lead 500/day is the documented cap in the cited article; org-specific increases are Needs verification.
security_notes: Web-to-Lead is unauthenticated capture; validate email and do not expose hidden privileged fields on the public form.
Opportunity product access requires the documented object permissions.
Never use real customer emails in LAB_ examples.
common_mistakes: Calling a Lead 'just a Contact we have not converted in our heads.'
Always creating an Opportunity on convert.
Forgetting Map Lead Fields for custom fields.
Adding products without a Price Book.

troubleshooting.symptom: Web-to-Lead creates no Lead or always hits the default owner.
check: Daily 500 cap in the cited Help
troubleshooting.do_not_assume: The HTML form is 'broken' before checking assignment and owner.

troubleshooting.symptom: Converted Account missing custom values from the Lead.
check: Map Lead Fields for that custom field
Whether the field is standard (standard mapping is not the custom mapper)

troubleshooting.symptom: Cannot add products to the Opportunity.
check: Read on Products and Price Books; Edit on Opportunities
troubleshooting.do_not_assume: Products tab visibility equals Price Book access.

production_notes: Map fields and test conversion in sandbox with LAB_ data before go-live.
Do not enable Person Accounts from a hallway request; it changes the data model.
Confirm Quotes license/edition before promising quote records to sales.

mcqs.prompt: According to Salesforce Help, about how many new leads can Web-to-Lead generate per day?
mcqs.rationale: Guidelines for Setting Up Web-to-Lead states the feature generates up to 500 new leads a day.

distractor_explanations.D: The cap is on web-generated leads, not opportunities.

mcqs.prompt: If the Lead assignment rule is inactive, who gets web-generated leads?

options.A: The default owner specified in Lead Settings
options.B: Always the user who last modified Setup
options.D: They convert automatically to Person Accounts

mcqs.rationale: Web-to-Lead Help: if the assignment rule is inactive, web-generated leads go to the default owner in Lead Settings.

mcqs.prompt: A custom field on Lead does not appear on Account after conversion. What should you check first?

options.A: Map Lead Fields for that custom field to Account
options.C: Whether the Price Book is standard

mcqs.rationale: Web-to-Lead / conversion guidance: create custom lead fields and specify how they map to Account, Contact, and Opportunity.

distractor_explanations.B: Quotes are unrelated to lead field maps.
distractor_explanations.C: Price books price products, not lead fields.
distractor_explanations.D: Campaign membership is not conversion mapping.

mcqs.prompt: What object permissions does Help require to add or edit opportunity products?

options.A: Edit on opportunities AND Read on products and price books

mcqs.rationale: Add Products to Opportunities lists Edit on opportunities and Read on products and price books.

distractor_explanations.B: Modify All Data is not the cited requirement.

mcqs.prompt: When you add the first product to an Opportunity, what must you choose?

options.A: A Price Book for the opportunity

mcqs.rationale: Help: if you are adding the first product, choose a price book for the opportunity.

distractor_explanations.B: Campaigns do not price opportunity lines.
distractor_explanations.D: Quote templates are a later quoting step.

mcqs.prompt: Where does the default sales price on an opportunity product come from?

options.A: The list price in the related Price Book

mcqs.rationale: Sales price defaults to the list price specified in the price book related to the opportunity.

distractor_explanations.B: Leads do not supply opportunity product list price.
distractor_explanations.D: Account revenue is not the SKU list price.

mcqs.prompt: Why create a custom Price Book?

options.A: To offer different prices to different market segments
options.B: To convert Leads without mapping fields

mcqs.rationale: Create Custom Price Books: create books for each market segment and add products with the prices you offer each segment.

distractor_explanations.C: Price books do not replace campaigns.
distractor_explanations.D: Price books do not control Person Accounts.

mcqs.prompt: Person Accounts are enabled. Lead Company is blank. What conversion outcome matches documented B2C behavior?

options.A: Person Account (not a separate business Account plus Contact for that human)
options.B: Always a business Account named '[not provided]'

mcqs.rationale: With Person Accounts, blank Company is the convert path to Person Account; Company populated converts to business Account. Mark exact UI labels Needs verification per org, but do not invent a Quote/Campaign conversion target.

distractor_explanations.B: Placeholder company text is a Web-to-Lead behavior when Person Accounts are off, not the Person Account convert target.

mcqs.prompt: A newsletter signup should be tracked for a spring promo but is not a sales deal. Where does it belong?

options.A: Lead (and Campaign member), not an Opportunity
options.C: A custom Price Book named Newsletter

mcqs.rationale: Lead is the capture object; Campaign holds members. Opportunity is for revenue deals.

distractor_explanations.D: Quotes are offers, not mailing lists.

mcqs.prompt: Which statement best separates Quote from Price Book?

options.A: A Price Book is the rate card; a Quote is a customer-facing offer and is edition-gated
options.B: They are the same object with two tabs

mcqs.rationale: Custom Price Books set segment prices; Help lists Quotes as not available in every edition.

distractor_explanations.D: Lead conversion is not a price book function.

mcqs.prompt: What does selecting Active on a custom Price Book allow?

options.A: Sales reps can add the price book or its entries to opportunities or quotes

mcqs.rationale: Create Custom Price Books: select Active to allow reps to begin adding the price book or its entries to opportunities or quotes.

distractor_explanations.B: Active does not change Web-to-Lead caps.

mcqs.prompt: Users who convert leads become the new lead owner. Which Lead Setting prevents Lead Status from flipping to the new owner's default?
mcqs.rationale: Lead Settings: to prevent Lead Status from changing to the new owner's default value, select Preserve Lead Status.

distractor_explanations.C: LinkedIn sync is a different setting.

flashcards.front: What is a Lead in Sales Cloud?
flashcards.back: A pre-relationship inquiry record. It is not yet the Account/Contact (or Person Account) customer model.

flashcards.front: What can Lead conversion create or match?
flashcards.back: Account and Contact, or a Person Account, and optionally an Opportunity.

flashcards.front: Person Accounts on, Company blank on convert?
flashcards.back: Convert to a Person Account. Company populated converts to a business Account plus Contact.
Up to 500 new leads a day per the cited Salesforce Help article.

flashcards.front: Inactive Lead assignment rule—who owns web leads?
flashcards.back: The default owner in Lead Settings.

flashcards.front: Custom Lead field missing after convert?
flashcards.back: Use Map Lead Fields to Account, Contact, and/or Opportunity before converting.
A Price Book for that Opportunity, plus Read on products and price books.
The list price from the Price Book entry related to the Opportunity.
Different list prices for different market segments (for example domestic vs international).
No. Help lists Performance and Developer, and Professional/Enterprise/Unlimited with Sales Cloud.
Members: leads, contacts, or person accounts—not a substitute for Opportunity revenue.

flashcards.front: What does Preserve Lead Status do?
flashcards.back: Stops Lead Status from changing to the converting user's default when they become owner.
Stay on Lead and Campaign membership. Do not auto-create an Opportunity.
Price Book is the internal rate card. Quote is the customer-facing offer record.

flashcards.front: Is converting a Lead metadata or data?
flashcards.back: Data: it creates/matches records. Field maps and Price Books are metadata.

interview_questions.question: Walk through Lead, conversion, Account, Contact, and Person Account.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: A Lead is a pre-customer inquiry. Conversion creates or matches Account and Contact, or a Person Account when Company is blank and Person Accounts are enabled. Opportunity is optional and should mean a real deal.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I keep Lead for capture and nurturing, including Web-to-Lead with its documented 500/day cap and default owner. I map custom fields before convert. Company present means business Account plus Contact. Blank Company with Person Accounts means Person Account. I do not convert newsletter noise into Opportunities. Account/Contact/Person Account rows are data; Lead Settings and field maps are metadata.
interview_questions.example: LAB_Maya blank Company becomes a Person Account; LAB_Northwind with Company becomes Account plus Contact.
tradeoffs: Lead capture quality vs premature conversion
Person Account model vs business Account plus Contact
follow_ups: Can you disable Person Accounts later? (Mark Needs verification.)
weak_answer_warnings: Saying Lead and Contact are the same object
Always creating an Opportunity on convert

interview_questions.question: How do Products, Price Books, and Quotes relate to an Opportunity?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Products are SKUs. A Price Book is the rate card; the first opportunity product chooses it. Sales price defaults from list price. A Quote is a customer-facing offer and is not in every edition.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I never type SKUs only in Description if we sell catalog items. Help requires Edit on Opportunities and Read on Products and Price Books. Custom Price Books exist for segments. Quotes are gated in the Price Book Help edition table. CPQ is a different product; I do not pretend standard Quotes equal CPQ.
interview_questions.example: LAB_Northwind Opportunity uses LAB_Corporate 2026 price book and LAB_CorporatePack quantity 10.
tradeoffs: One standard book vs many custom books
follow_ups: What if Amount should roll up from products?

interview_questions.question: Marketing wants every web form to create an Opportunity in Prospecting. What do you say?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I refuse that default. Web-to-Lead should create Leads. Opportunity is for a deal. Use Campaign membership for the promo audience.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I explain forecast pollution: fake Opportunities wreck pipeline reporting in APP-002. I offer Lead plus Campaign, assignment rules, and conversion when sales qualifies. I mention the 500/day web cap and default owner so they do not think the form is unlimited CRM. I still map fields so conversion is clean later.
interview_questions.example: LAB_Spring Promo campaign members from Web-to-Lead; convert only after a booked demo.
tradeoffs: Marketing vanity metrics vs sales pipeline integrity
Speed of 'everything is a deal' vs data quality
follow_ups: What Lead Status means qualified here?
weak_answer_warnings: Agreeing to auto-Opportunity without a deal

interview_questions.question: B2C org enables Person Accounts. What conversion rule do you teach reps?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Blank Company converts to Person Account. Company filled converts to business Account plus Contact. Do not invent dummy companies just to force B2B shape.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I check whether Person Accounts are already on before touching production. I explain Web-to-Lead Company behavior changes when Person Accounts are enabled (Company not universally required). I keep Opportunity optional. I warn that mixing dummy 'Lastname Household' business Accounts with Person Accounts destroys reporting. Enablement details get a Needs verification look at current Help.
interview_questions.example: Gym member Maya with no company → Person Account; corporate Northwind → Account and Contact.
tradeoffs: True B2C model vs fake B2B accounts
follow_ups: What happens to Contacts already in the org?
weak_answer_warnings: Treating Person Account as a Contact record type only

interview_questions.question: Converted Account is missing the custom source field from the Lead. Diagnose.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Open Map Lead Fields. Custom fields do not copy unless mapped. Standard-to-standard mapping is not the same tool.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I reproduce with a LAB_ lead. I confirm the Account field exists and FLS. I check the map. I do not write a Flow 'because conversion is broken' until the map is proven empty. Process Builder workarounds for standard fields are legacy; I would prefer documented mapping plus a modern Flow only if Help still says standard fields cannot use the mapper.
interview_questions.example: LAB_Channel__c on Lead unmapped; Account stays blank after convert.
tradeoffs: Standard field limits vs custom fields
follow_ups: Can you map one Lead field to two parents?

interview_questions.question: Rep cannot add products to an Opportunity. Walk the checks.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Check Edit on Opportunities and Read on Products and Price Books. Confirm an Active Price Book and that this is the first-product price book choice.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I distinguish tab visibility from object permissions. I confirm the book is Active so it can be used on opportunities or quotes. I check whether the org even has products. I do not jump to CPQ. If Quotes are missing entirely, I read the edition table rather than 'fixing' Setup blindly.
interview_questions.example: Standard User lacks Read on Price Book; Add Products never appears.
weak_answer_warnings: Telling them to type Amount instead

interview_questions.question: When would you not use a Campaign for this topic's job?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When the need is a priced deal, SKUs, or a customer-facing Quote. Campaigns are member rosters, not Opportunities or Price Books.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I use Campaigns to track who was targeted in LAB_Spring Promo. I use Opportunity plus Price Book for revenue. I use Quote when the edition supports a formal offer. Mixing them makes ROI and pipeline reports lie. Campaign Influence is a later feature; I do not fake it with extra Opportunities.
interview_questions.example: Email clickers stay Campaign members; only booked demos become Opportunities.
weak_answer_warnings: Using Campaign as the quote object

interview_questions.question: Teach the sales object map without saying 'it's just CRM.'
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Freight depot: Lead is the crate in receiving, conversion is customs, Account/Contact or Person Account are consignee records, Opportunity is the booked lane, Price Book is the rate card, Quote is the printed offer, Campaign is the promo roster.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I then break the analogy: conversion may match existing customers; Person Accounts are an org model; Quotes are licensed; Campaigns do not carry SKU lines. I mention Web-to-Lead 500/day and Map Lead Fields so the interviewer hears official Help, not a story. I keep metadata (maps, books, settings) separate from LAB_ records.
interview_questions.example: Whiteboard: two leads, two convert outcomes, one price-booked opportunity, one campaign.
weak_answer_warnings: Generic catalog metaphors instead of the freight-depot mapping
